rv.q: Powered by a notably youthful cast — many look as if they had just cleared the Clearasil years — the production, directed by Bob Moss, has a sunny-spirited exuberance that quickly fills the intimate East 13th Street Theater (better known as home to the Classic Stage Company).

The first full scale New York revival and the first Off Broadway production ever, The Berkshire Theatre Group’s staging of the Bock & Harnick musical, Fiorello!, has moved to New York’s East 13th Street Theater from Stockbridge, Massachusetts.
Quibbles aside, this is a production that no fan of classic musical theater will want to miss, nor anyone who wants to see the future stars of New York theater before they really hit it big.
The BTG's transfer is sweet, lively and timely.
Under the direction of Bob Moss (the founder of Playwrights Horizons), the production is full of tender emotion, dramatically effective and highly enjoyable.
If you're in the mood for a good old-fashioned (literally flag-waving) American musical, this is your ticket.

"A rewarding evening—but one where you may find yourself making allowances...It’s still a gripping political and romantic tale...And, bless us all, it’s all punctuated with the music of Jerry Bock and the lyrics of Sheldon Harnick...It’s a youthful cast, sometimes disconcertingly so...Director Bob Moss might want to encourage his cast to dig...
While this new mounting isn't a bad one, it's essentially a college-level production charging Off-Broadway prices.
Down here on 13th Street, it seems--well, a welcome way to form an acquaintance with Bock & Harnick's Pulitzer-winner but not exactly up to professional standards.
Republican or not, if Fiorello LaGuardia were running for office today, I’d be more likely to vote for him than for this underage revival of his life story.
It's a handsome piece, filled with talented young people, but it would have been better left in the Berkshire Hills.
But the musical feels like a summer-stock production by college students just eager to put on a show.
The show is warm, tuneful, charming, wry, and wise. You'll have a good time.
Quibbles aside, this is a production that no fan of classic musical theater will want to miss.
The clever songs and lyrics keep the audience enamored, the timeliness of political corruption – always on the money (no pun intended).
This show works for all the reasons musical theater does when it’s well executed.
Whatever quibbles one may find here, this staging is an admirable, welcomely enjoyable opportunity to see this show.

It's still terrifically charming and enjoyable, though, and expect to see the careers of Austin Scott Lombardi (Fiorello), Katie Birenboim (Marie), and Matt McLean (his other long-suffering assistant, Morris) flourish in the future.
Sure, it's far from perfect but you will still have a very good time and be glad you went.
Originally performed in 1959, this story of New York Mayor Fiorello H. LaGuardia struggles—and sometimes succeeds—in finding relevancy nearly sixty years later.
Fiorello himself, Austin Scott Lombardi, is a bit of a disappointment, unfortunately.
As the director of this revival, Robert Moss — whom the NYC theater community fondly remembers for founding Playwrights Horizons — lacks Abbott’s knack.
For good and for bad, this Off-Broadway revival of Fiorello! tingles with an eager, fresh-faced youthfulness from start to finish.
The problem with this show coming from Berkshire Theatre Group’s home in Stockbridge, Mass. is that the cast is extremely young and it feels like a non-union college production.
I am afraid this production is only for the die-hard fans of the musical.
This production is nowhere near on that level, but it reminds on how good FIORELLO's score is.

cn.t: Critics find this Bock and Harnick revival charming and timely, praising its talented young cast and splendid score, though some note the dated book and question whether the performers look too youthful for their roles.
